vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded API Key
vulnerabilities.description: API key is hardcoded in source code as 'AKIA_EXAMPLE_HARDCODED_KEY_123456'. This exposes sensitive credentials to anyone with access to the repository.
remediation_steps: Move API key to environment variables
Add .env file to .gitignore
Use a secrets management system in production
Rotate the hardcoded key immediately

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Direct string formatting used in SQL query allows attackers to inject arbitrary SQL commands through the 'name' parameter.
vulnerabilities.vulnerable_code: sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE '%{}%'".format(name)
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement:
sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?"
cur.execute(sql, (f'%{name}%',))
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements)
Never concatenate user input into SQL strings
Use ORM frameworks like SQLAlchemy for additional protection
Validate and sanitize all user inputs

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle)
vulnerabilities.description: Using pickle.loads() on user-controlled data enables arbitrary code execution. Pickle can deserialize and execute malicious Python objects.
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement:
data = request.get_json()
if not data:
    return jsonify({"error": "Invalid JSON"}), 400
profile = data
remediation_steps: Replace pickle with JSON for untrusted data
Implement strict input validation
Use safe deserialization libraries
Never deserialize data from untrusted sources

vulnerabilities.title: OS Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly concatenated into os.system() call, allowing command injection attacks.
remediation_steps: Use subprocess module instead of os.system()
Pass commands as list of arguments (not string)
Implement timeout protection
Never concatenate user input into shell commands

vulnerabilities.title: Server-Side Template Injection
vulnerabilities.description: User input is directly embedded into template string passed to render_template_string(), enabling template injection attacks.
remediation_steps: Use template variables instead of string formatting
Rely on Jinja2's auto-escaping feature
Never dynamically construct template strings with user input
Use static templates from files when possible
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Templating Engine

vulnerabilities.title: Weak Password Storage
vulnerabilities.description: Passwords are stored in plaintext and compared using direct equality. No hashing or salting is used.
remediation_steps: Use werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash() for password hashing
Use werkzeug.security.check_password_hash() for verification
Never store plaintext passwords
Consider bcrypt or argon2 for additional security
Implement password policies and validation
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

vulnerabilities.title: Debug Mode Enabled in Production
vulnerabilities.description: Flask debug mode is enabled, exposing sensitive information like stack traces, environment variables, and interactive debugging.
remediation_steps: Disable debug mode in production
Use environment variables to control debug status
Implement proper logging instead of debug mode
Never expose stack traces to end users

summary.recommendation: All vulnerabilities should be addressed immediately, especially critical severity items. Implement the provided secure replacements and deploy a new version of the application.
